skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // FixedSizeBumpAllocator - Specifications
5. //
6. // This file contains the abstract View (`BumpView`), its invariant and geometry
7. // helpers, the numeric specification of `align_up`, and the proof-lemma targets
8. // that encode the caller expectations. See
9. // `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-bump-allocator/view_design.md` for the design
10. // rationale.
11. //
12. // NOTE: Attaching `BumpView` as the `View` of `FixedSizeBumpAllocator` is a later
13. // phase (view_design.md, end of section 2). It requires an atomic-ghost / PointsTo
14. // token to model the interior-mutable `AtomicUsize` cursor, because the raw atomic
15. // value is not readable in spec (vstd: "NO support for reasoning about the values
16. // inside the atomics"). Until then `BumpView` is referenced by the proof lemmas in
17. // `lib.proof.rs`, which state the caller-facing guarantees over the abstract pool.
18. 
19. verus! {
20. 
21. //==================================================================================================
22. // std-library specifications not yet covered by vstd
23. //==================================================================================================
24. 
25. // `usize::div_ceil` rounds the quotient towards positive infinity. It panics on a
26. // zero divisor, hence the `y != 0` precondition. For unsigned operands the result
27. // never overflows, and equals `ceil(x / y) == (x + y - 1) / y`.
28. pub assume_specification [ <usize>::div_ceil ](x: usize, y: usize) -> (result: usize)
29.     requires
30.         y != 0,
31.     ensures
32.         result as int == (x as int + y as int - 1) / (y as int),
33. ;
34. 
35. //==================================================================================================
36. // align_up - numeric specification
37. //==================================================================================================
38. 
39. /// Least multiple of `alignment` that is `>= value`; `None` when `alignment == 0`
40. /// or when that multiple does not fit in a `usize`.
41. ///
42. /// This is the View-independent numeric meaning of `align_up`. The allocator's
43. /// `stride` (see `BumpView::inv`) is pinned to this function.
44. pub open spec fn align_up_spec(value: nat, alignment: nat) -> Option<nat> {
45.     if alignment == 0 {
46.         None
47.     } else {
48.         let m: int = ((value + alignment - 1) / (alignment as int)) * (alignment as int);
49.         if m > usize::MAX as int {
50.             None
51.         } else {
52.             Some(m as nat)
53.         }
54.     }
55. }
56. 
57. //==================================================================================================
58. // BumpView - abstract pool model
59. //==================================================================================================
60. 
61. /// Abstract view of a `FixedSizeBumpAllocator<N, A, S>`.
62. ///
63. /// Pure ghost description of the slot pool: no atomics, no raw pointers, no cursor
64. /// mechanism. Carries the fixed pool geometry plus the single dynamic quantity
65. /// `allocated` (the number of slots handed out so far).
66. #[verifier::ext_equal]
67. pub struct BumpView {
68.     /// Base address of the backing region (`S::as_mut_ptr()` as an integer).
69.     pub base: int,
70.     /// Distance in bytes between consecutive slots (`align_up(unit_size, unit_align)`).
71.     pub stride: nat,
72.     /// Size of each slot in bytes (the const generic `N`).
73.     pub unit_size: nat,
74.     /// Required alignment of each slot in bytes (the const generic `A`).
75.     pub unit_align: nat,
76.     /// Number of slots the pool can ever yield (`S::NUM_UNITS`).
77.     pub capacity: nat,
78.     /// Total size in bytes of the backing region (`S::STORAGE_SIZE`).
79.     pub storage_size: nat,
80.     /// Number of slots already handed out. The only dynamic field.
81.     pub allocated: nat,
82. }
83. 
84. impl BumpView {
85.     /// Address of slot `i` (0-based). The pool's geometry, independent of the
86.     /// allocation mechanism.
87.     pub open spec fn slot_addr(self, i: int) -> int {
88.         self.base + i * (self.stride as int)
89.     }
90. 
91.     /// A slot index is *consumed* iff it is below the high-water mark.
92.     pub open spec fn is_consumed(self, i: int) -> bool {
93.         0 <= i < self.allocated
94.     }
95. 
96.     /// The allocator still has at least one free slot.
97.     pub open spec fn has_capacity(self) -> bool {
98.         self.allocated < self.capacity
99.     }
100. 
101.     /// Well-formedness of the abstract pool. Each clause backs a caller-visible
102.     /// guarantee (see `view_design.md` section 3).
103.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
104.         // (a) Geometry is well formed: non-empty, non-overlapping slots.
105.         &&& self.unit_size > 0
106.         &&& self.unit_align > 0
107.         &&& self.stride >= self.unit_size
108.         // (b) Stride is the up-alignment of the unit size to the unit alignment,
109.         //     and every slot start inherits `unit_align` from an aligned base.
110.         &&& align_up_spec(self.unit_size, self.unit_align) == Some(self.stride)
111.         &&& (self.stride as int) % (self.unit_align as int) == 0
112.         &&& self.base % (self.unit_align as int) == 0
113.         // (c) The pool fits inside the backing region.
114.         &&& (self.capacity as int) * (self.stride as int) <= self.storage_size as int
115.         // (d) Addresses do not wrap the usize space.
116.         &&& self.base >= 0
117.         &&& self.base + (self.storage_size as int) <= usize::MAX as int + 1
118.         // (e) Monotone-capacity ceiling.
119.         &&& self.allocated <= self.capacity
120.     }
121. 
122.     /// The three geometric guarantees the kernel's `unsafe` soundness relies on,
123.     /// stated over the whole pool: every slot is aligned, in-bounds, and distinct.
124.     pub open spec fn geometry_ok(self) -> bool {
125.         &&& (forall|i: int|
126.             0 <= i < self.capacity ==> #[trigger] self.slot_addr(i) % (self.unit_align as int) == 0)
127.         &&& (forall|i: int|
128.             0 <= i < self.capacity ==> {
129.                 &&& self.base <= #[trigger] self.slot_addr(i)
130.                 &&& self.slot_addr(i) + (self.unit_size as int) <= self.base + (self.storage_size
131.                     as int)
132.             })
133.         &&& (forall|i: int, j: int|
134.             (0 <= i < self.capacity && 0 <= j < self.capacity && i != j)
135.                 ==> (#[trigger] self.slot_addr(i)) != (#[trigger] self.slot_addr(j)))
136.     }
137. 
138.     /// Abstract transition performed by a successful allocation: one more slot is
139.     /// consumed, nothing else changes.
140.     pub open spec fn spec_alloc(self) -> BumpView {
141.         BumpView { allocated: (self.allocated + 1) as nat, ..self }
142.     }
143. }
144. 
145. } // verus!
146.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // FixedSizeBumpAllocator - Proofs
5. //
6. // Proof-function signatures for the abstract pool model. Bodies are `admit()`
7. // placeholders during the specification phase; the proving phase discharges them.
8. // Each lemma encodes a caller expectation from
9. // `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-bump-allocator/caller_analysis.md`.
10. 
11. verus! {
12. 
13. //==================================================================================================
14. // Geometry lemmas (uniqueness / in-bounds / alignment)
15. //==================================================================================================
16. 
17. /// A well-formed pool satisfies all three geometric guarantees: every slot is
18. /// `unit_align`-aligned, lies fully inside the backing region, and is distinct
19. /// from every other slot.
20. ///
21. /// Backs caller invariants: *Alignment*, *In-bounds*, *Uniqueness / non-aliasing*.
22. pub proof fn lemma_geometry(v: BumpView)
23.     requires
24.         v.inv(),
25.     ensures
26.         v.geometry_ok(),
27. {
28.     admit();
29. }
30. 
31. //==================================================================================================
32. // Capacity / transition lemmas (monotone capacity, no spurious consumption)
33. //==================================================================================================
34. 
35. /// The exhaustion boundary is exactly `allocated == capacity`: the pool has a free
36. /// slot iff fewer than `capacity` slots have been handed out.
37. ///
38. /// Backs caller invariant: *Monotone capacity* (the `Exhausted` boundary).
39. pub proof fn lemma_exhausted_boundary(v: BumpView)
40.     requires
41.         v.inv(),
42.     ensures
43.         !v.has_capacity() <==> v.allocated == v.capacity,
44. {
45.     admit();
46. }
47. 
48. /// A successful allocation advances the cursor by exactly one slot and preserves
49. /// the invariant. The freshly handed-out index `v.allocated` was previously free
50. /// and becomes consumed.
51. ///
52. /// Backs caller invariants: *Monotone capacity* (advance by one), *Uniqueness*
53. /// (each index handed out at most once).
54. pub proof fn lemma_alloc_transition(v: BumpView)
55.     requires
56.         v.inv(),
57.         v.has_capacity(),
58.     ensures
59.         v.spec_alloc().inv(),
60.         v.spec_alloc().allocated == v.allocated + 1,
61.         !v.is_consumed(v.allocated as int),
62.         v.spec_alloc().is_consumed(v.allocated as int),
63.         // Configuration (everything except `allocated`) is unchanged.
64.         v.spec_alloc() == (BumpView { allocated: v.spec_alloc().allocated, ..v }),
65. {
66.     admit();
67. }
68. 
69. } // verus!
70.
